incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: British Virgin Islands Business Companies Act, 2004 (as amended), ss. 5-9 (incorporation) and s. 96 (board resolutions); UK Companies Act 2006, Part 34 (ss. 1046-1060) and the Overseas Companies Regulations 2009 (SI 2009/1917); retained UK Medical Devices Regulations 2002 (SI 2002/618) for device establishment licensing
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs (RCA) via licensed registered agent; UK Companies House (Registrar of Companies for England and Wales) for overseas establishment registration
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: BVI Certificate of Incorporation issued upon filing of Memorandum and Articles of Association and Form BTC1; UK Form OSIN01 (Application for Registration of a UK Establishment) for Companies House
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a BVI Business Company (minimum capital requirement expressly waived); shares may be issued with no par value; initial subscription proceeds, if any, must be credited to the company's bank account with evidence retained for AML review; no escrow account is mandated under the Business Companies Act
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: Whereas the Company was incorporated with one subscriber, the first board hereby (1) ratifies the subscribers' allotment of 10,000 ordinary no-par-value shares at US$1.00 per share; (2) adopts as registered office the address notified to the BVI Registrar and appoints the licensed registered agent; (3) appoints the initial directors and the corporate secretary as set out in the register; (4) authorises opening of bank accounts in the United Kingdom and approval of the proposed signatories; (5) directs the registered agent to file the UK establishment registration with Companies House; (6) authorises management to obtain the MHRA establishment registration, environmental permit, fire safety certificate and occupational health clearance. Any one director may sign all ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Pre-Filing Sanctions Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs (RCA) - MyVICORE online portal via licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a BVI-licensed corporate services provider as registered agent. Submit the proposed corporate name through the MyVICORE name-approval module using the suffix 'Limited' or 'BVI Business Company'. Complete the AML/KYC and sanctions screening of the ultimate beneficial owner before the name application is filed. Obtain the name reservation certificate before proceeding to incorporation.
required_dossiers: BVI Name Reservation Application Form
UBO identification documents (passport and proof of residential address)
Corporate services engagement letter with the licensed registered agent
AML/Sanctions screening report for all natural person beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity or undesirability, resubmit with two alternative names or file a notarised letter of consent from the objecting company; request administrative review within 14 calendar days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BVI Registry of Corporate Affairs (RCA) - Companies Registration Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the Memorandum and Articles of Association, Form BTC1, the registered agent's declaration, and the registered office consent letter through MyVICORE. Pay the official incorporation fee and first-year license fee online via the registered agent's pre-funded account. The Registrar will issue the Certificate of Incorporation and certified copy of the Articles of Association.
required_dossiers: BVI Incorporation Form BTC1
Memorandum and Articles of Association (drafted by registered agent)
Registered Agent Declaration (Form BVI-RA-1)
Registered Office Consent Letter
Approved name reservation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues an objection or query, file a corrective submission under section 9 of the Business Companies Act within 21 days; request priority re-processing upon resolution of the name or document defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Initial Share Allotment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors acting under section 96 of the BVI Business Companies Act, 2004
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Call the inaugural board meeting at the registered office in Road Town, Tortola. Adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution. Issue the 10,000 ordinary shares subscribed by the founding shareholder and record the allotment in the Register of Members. Execute share certificates and have minutes signed by the chair.
required_dossiers: Notice of First Board Meeting
Pro-Forma First Board Resolution (as set out in the legal framework)
Register of Members
Share certificates for 10,000 ordinary no-par-value shares
Written consent of the subscriber to allotment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director is unavailable, proceed by unanimous written resolution under section 96 without a physical meeting; if a bank queries the share issue, adopt a supplemental board consent confirming that cash consideration was received and credited.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registers, Registered Office, and Agent Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BVI Registered Agent (licensed under the Securities and Investment Business Act, 2001) and BVI RCA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the registered office agreement and file the registered agent's consent with the RCA. Maintain the statutory registers (members, directors, officers, and charges) at the agent's office. Deliver the Economic Substance Notification to the BVI International Tax Authority within the statutory deadline if the company carries on relevant activity in the BVI.
required_dossiers: Registered Office Consent Letter
Registered Agent Agreement
Statutory Registers (members, directors, officers, and charges)
Economic Substance Notification (if applicable)
Registered Agent AML compliance declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCA notifies a deficiency in the registers or agent declaration, cure by filing corrected registers within 10 business days; pay any late fee and request confirmation from the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: UK Overseas Establishment Registration with Companies House
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: UK Companies House (Registrar of Companies for England and Wales) - WebFiling portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare certified English translations of the BVI Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Association. File Form OSIN01, OSIN02, and OSIN03 online, appointing the UK registered office and identifying persons authorised to represent the BVI company. Pay the GBP 20 filing fee. Upon registration, the company receives a UK establishment number and becomes subject to annual filing duties.
required_dossiers: Form OSIN01 (application for registration of a UK establishment)
Form OSIN02 (UK registered office address)
Form OSIN03 (details of directors and secretary)
Certified English translation of BVI Certificate of Incorporation and Articles
Statement of initial significant control (PSC) based on the BVI register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Companies House rejects the filing for deficient translation or invalid address, re-file corrected OSIN01 within 7 days; maintain the payment receipt for fee apportionment; request expedited processing under the Companies House expedited service where operational urgency is demonstrated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening Corporate Bank Account and Activation of Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: UK-regulated bank or FCA-authorised Electronic Money Institution (EMI), subject to enhanced due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the BVI Certificate of Incorporation, UK establishment registration confirmation, beneficial ownership structure, and proposed payment rails (SWIFT wire and letters of credit). Undergo enhanced due diligence for the High-Risk manufacturing scope and medical device sector. Execute the corporate banking mandate and activate Swift Wire and Letter of Credit facilities.
required_dossiers: BVI Certificate of Incorporation (certified copy)
UK Companies House OSIN01 registration confirmation
UBO, source of wealth, and source of funds evidence
Board resolution approving signatories and banking mandate
Business plan and 3-year forecast for intraocular lens manufacturing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If account opening is paused or declined, file a regulatory risk mitigation memorandum from external counsel confirming the MHRA licensing pipeline, ISO 13485 certification plan, and enhanced AML controls; re-submit to an alternative FCA-regulated EMI or correspondent bank.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) - Devices Division and UK Approved Body (BSI Assurance UK Ltd) under retained Regulation (EU) 2017/745
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: MHRA Manufacturer Establishment Registration (Class III implantable medical device) and UKCA/CE Certificate of Conformity under retained MDR 2017/745, accompanied by ISO 13485 Quality Management System certification for sterile intraocular lens manufacture

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment Agency (England) / Natural Resources Wales / Scottish Environment Protection Agency (SEPA) depending on site location; default England
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 - Registration-tier environmental permit under the Environmental Permitting (England and Wales) Regulations 2016 (SI 2016/1154); Full EIA Report under the Town and Country Planning (Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations 2017 (SI 2017/571) Schedule 2 triggered only for new facilities exceeding 10,000 sq. m. floor area or those discharging to sensitive water receptors
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater effluent limits: pH 6-9, BOD not exceeding 20 mg/L, COD not exceeding 125 mg/L, total suspended solids not exceeding 30 mg/L, ammonia not exceeding 10 mg/L; fugitive VOC emissions below 5 tonnes per year with abatement controls; polymer offcuts and expired lenses classified as clinical waste (Chapter 18) under HTM 07-01; cleanroom air particulate control to ISO Class 5 (ISO 14644-1) for lens finishing operations

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate under the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005 with annual fire risk assessment; structural engineer's load inspection certificate for cleanroom flooring, mezzanine, and autoclave areas; HSE workplace clearance and occupational health surveillance for staff; Control of Substances Hazardous to Health (COSHH) assessments for methyl methacrylate monomer, polymer dust, and sterilisation agents; electrical and pressure systems inspection certificate

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC); official portal: www.gov.uk/topic/business-tax
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident BVI Business Company has no automatic UK tax registration obligation unless it acquires a UK permanent establishment, derives UK property income, employs UK staff, or makes taxable supplies in the UK. To obtain a statutory TIN/VAT ID: (1) apply to HMRC using form VAT1A (Registration of a non-established taxable person) to obtain a GB VAT registration number; (2) register for Corporation Tax through HMRC's 'Register a new company for Corporation Tax' online service to obtain a Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR) if a UK PE or trading presence arises; (3) obtain an EORI number (GB + 12 digits) via HMRC's customs portal before undertaking any import/export declarations; (4) register for PAYE if UK employees are engaged. The BVI BC's constitutional documents, registered office certificate, and proof of economic substance in BVI must accompany any registration application.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The BVI BC is tax-exempt under BVI domestic law (no income tax, corporation tax, capital gains tax, or VAT in the BVI). For UK tax purposes no 'check-the-box' election exists; statutory classification follows UK domestic rules: a foreign corporation is treated as opaque for Corporation Tax unless an anti-hybrid election applies under TIOPA 2010 Part 6A (e.g., election to treat a foreign transparent entity as opaque or apply switch-over rule) to counteract deduction/non-inclusion mismatches. Other available elections include: VAT margin scheme election for qualifying second-hand goods; option to tax (election for VAT on property, not applicable to goods); and election under CTA 2009 s.18A for loan relationships and derivative contracts. Where a UK-BVI double tax treaty is absent (no treaty in force), residence is tested solely by domestic law: central management and control (UK) determines UK corporate residence regardless of BVI incorporation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax) – UK national VAT regime
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: The UK statutory threshold is £90,000 taxable turnover in any 12-month rolling period for UK-established businesses; non-established overseas businesses (including BVI BCs) must register for UK VAT from their first taxable supply in the UK, unless the supply is zero-rated, exempt, or subject to a reverse charge. The distance-selling threshold of £8,818 applies only to consignment sales of goods located in the EU/Northern Ireland at the time of sale.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory mandate for real-time clearance, digital stamping, or fiscal pre-authorisation of invoices in the UK. E-invoicing is permitted and used voluntarily, but HMRC does not operate a continuous transaction control (CTC) system for VAT. Since April 2022, all VAT-registered businesses must keep digital records and submit VAT returns through Making Tax Digital (MTD) using HMRC-recognised software via the MTD Application Programming Interface (API). Customs declarations must be submitted electronically through the Customs Declaration Service (CDS); export declarations can be lodged via API-enabled systems or the UK 'Exports' digital service. Intrastat (EC Sales/Arrivals) returns for goods statistics require electronic filing where movement thresholds are exceeded.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of intraocular acrylic lenses to non-UK destinations is zero-rated under VATA 1994, Sch. 8, Group 7 (Exports) provided the goods are physically exported from the UK within three months of the supply, or within six months where removed under customs/duty suspension arrangements, and the supplier receives and preserves valid evidence of export, including a Customs Export Declaration, transport documents (Bill of Lading/Airway Bill), and commercial documentation showing the foreign destination and customer. Where the goods are sold to a UK VAT-registered customer for subsequent export, the supply may be zero-rated if both parties hold the prescribed evidence and conditions in SI 1995/2518 are met. Related services directly linked to the exported lenses (e.g., final assembly, quality testing) are zero-rated when the recipient belongs outside the UK.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic SAD via UK Customs Declaration Service, CDS)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (or CMR / rail consignment note for non-sea/air exports)
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT credit confirmation evidencing receipt of foreign currency
Certificate of Origin (issued by chambers of commerce, where the destination customs regime requires proof of UK/EU preference)
Medical Device Technical File / UKCA-CE marking evidence, if requested by customs authorities for intraocular lens imports
Export Licence (dual-use or healthcare-relevant restrictions only where applicable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: HMRC operates targeted assurance reviews of zero-rated exporters, particularly medical-device traders using intermediary corporate structures. If the export evidence is missing, incomplete, or false, the supply is recharacterised as standard-rated; VAT at 20% and statutory interest are assessed and clawed back retrospectively. Civil penalties arise under Sch. 24 FA 2007: careless inaccuracy 0-30%; deliberate inaccuracy 20-70%; deliberate and concealed inaccuracy 30-100% of the VAT lost. Criminal prosecution for dishonest evasion of VAT under VATA 1994 s.72 and FA 2000 s.144 carries imprisonment of up to 7 years and/or unlimited fines; the court may also impose director disqualification and confiscation orders under POCA 2002. Retrospective clawback periods: HMRC standard assessment window is 4 years; the window extends to 6 years in the case of careless conduct and 20 years for deliberate non-disclosure/offshore arrangements. Concurrent customs penalties under the Taxation (Cross-border Trade) Act 2018 may reach 100% of the value of the goods plus forfeiture of the consignment; a fraudulent exporter also loses eligibility for the Authorised Economic Operator (AEO) status, triggering 100% physical examination rates.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (monetary authority); HM Treasury oversees exchange control policy; no separate foreign exchange administration exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for current and capital account transactions. No exchange control restrictions on profit remittance, dividends, or capital repatriation. UK applies no blocking codes under the Foreign Exchange Act; post-Brexit, real-time gross settlement in GBP via CHAPS.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds or convert foreign currency to GBP. Exporters may retain balances in any currency; reporting only for trade statistics via Intrastat/EC Sales List (EU exit adjustments).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Legal basis under UK Electronic Money Regulations 2011 (EMR). Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Revolut Business, Wise Business, MultiPass) may offer GBP/IBAN accounts but often refuse high-risk medical manufacturing. EDD enhanced scrutiny; requires UK registered address and economically linked activity to avoid de-risking.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote video onboarding is statutorily permissible under the Money Laundering Regulations 2017 (MLR 2017) where a risk-based approach is adopted. However, for a BVI BC with a high-risk ISIC 3250 scope, most UK Tier-1 banks mandate a physical attendance of at least one director or UBO (alternatively via a UK-registered agent) for initial account opening and sanction/reputation risk assessment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex structure with offshore BVI holding and UK operational nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organizational chart, certificate of incorporation, register of directors/members, beneficial ownership statement (PSC), proof of economic substance in UK (lease, payroll, VAT registration), and patent/regulatory licenses (MHRA, CE).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction indicators due to ultimate beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO passports, proof of funds, source of wealth statements, CVs of directors, independent reference letters from a regulated lawyer/accountant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Product class (intraocular acrylic lenses) considered sensitive medical device
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISO 13485 certificate, CE marking (MDD 93/42/EEC), MHRA registration, clinical trial certification, insurance policies (product liability), and purchase agreements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injection from BVI holding must be routed via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'E110' (Investment in the UK) under Bank of England statistics. Verification includes board resolution, proof of funds, and source of wealth. For trade invoices, use commercial purpose codes; all inbound funds subject to 14-day AML screening and FCA transfer of funds regulations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: SWIFT MT103 for open account payments to suppliers; Documentary Letters of Credit (MT700) for high-value acrylic polymer purchases; UK settlement via CHAPS for GBP, via TARGET2 for EUR, via SWIFT for USD. All payments subject to FCA Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2017. LC advised through a UK confirming bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward up to 12 months under FCA conduct of business rules
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with low liquidity, but for GBP-USD/EUR active market
Cross-currency swaps for GBP/USD/EUR, subject to ISDA master agreement and EMIR reporting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation Statement (Form CS01) — confirmation of registered details and Persons with Significant Control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every 12 months on the confirmation date, being the anniversary of incorporation or of the company's registration in the UK; online filing is open during the 14 days ending on that date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-delivery is a criminal offence; the company and officers in default are liable to fines up to £5,000 and daily default fines. The Registrar may initiate involuntary strike-off after 28 days' notice where filings are repeatedly outstanding.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Audit Report (Companies Act 2006, Part 15 / Part 34)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a UK private company, within 9 months after the end of the accounting reference period; for an overseas (BVI-incorporated) company with a UK establishment, within 13 months after the end of the accounting reference period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic late-filing penalties apply, rising from £150 for a private company up to £1,500 where accounts are over six months late; penalties double on repeated default. Directors may be disqualified and Companies House may strike off the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UK Register of Overseas Entities (ROE) Annual Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies House / Registrar of Overseas Entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each 12-month anniversary of the overseas entity's registration in the ROE; Companies House normally issues a reminder 14 days before the 60-day filing window expires.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is a criminal offence; daily default fines up to £2,500 may be imposed on the entity and each officer in default. The entity is restricted from acquiring, leasing or charging qualifying UK land until the annual update is delivered.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BVI Annual Government Fee and Registered Agent Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BVI Financial Services Commission via the BVI registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 May, or the anniversary-based renewal date specified by the BVI Business Companies Act; the BVI registered agent issues the renewal invoice in advance of the statutory deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment by the due date triggers late fees and may result in the company's removal from the BVI register and loss of separate legal personality. Reinstatement requires payment of all arrears, penalties and renewed registered agent consent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UK Corporation Tax Return (Form CT600), Tax Computation and Supporting Schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the accounting period; where HMRC issues a notice to file, no later than 3 months after the date of the notice, whichever is later.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an automatic £100 penalty, escalating daily penalties up to £1,500 and tax-geared penalties up to 100% of the liability. Interest accrues on unpaid corporation tax and HMRC may issue estimated assessments and pursue enforcement action.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit is mandatory in the UK where a company is public, is in a regulated financial services sector, or exceeds two of the following small company thresholds: turnover above £10.2 million, gross balance-sheet total above £5.1 million, or average employees above 50. Medium company thresholds are turnover above £15.9 million, gross balance-sheet total above £7.9 million and average employees above 250. A BVI Business Company operating through a UK establishment is subject to the same audit requirement unless a Part 34 Companies Act 2006 exemption applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: UK adopted International Accounting Standards (IFRS) apply to public-interest entities; FRS 101 or FRS 102 (UK GAAP) are available for eligible non-public-interest companies. A BVI-incorporated entity filing under the Companies (Accounts) Regulations may deliver financial statements prepared under IFRS or an equivalent recognised accounting framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For the BVI Business Company, a beneficial ownership register must be maintained with the BVI registered agent and reported to the BVI Beneficial Ownership Secure Search System (BOSS); changes arising from share transfers must be notified within 14 days. For UK purposes, the ROE annual update must be filed within 60 days of each annual update date, and a UK incorporated entity must certify its PSC register through the Annual Confirmation Statement. All shareholding transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members before the annual confirmation is submitted.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$450–US$1,200 per annum for UK registered office and company secretarial services; US$1,200–US$2,500 per annum for the BVI registered agent.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$12,000–US$35,000 per annum for a mid-size medical device manufacturer requiring a certified statutory audit under UK GAAP or IFRS.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: UK Corporation Tax main rate 25% (FY2024/FY2025). Small Profits Rate 19% for profits ≤ £50,000; marginal relief applies between £50,000 and £250,000 with effective rates 19%–25%. A BVI BC with a UK permanent establishment is chargeable on PE-attributable profits (CTA 2009 s.19); the BVI itself imposes 0% corporate income tax on the BC.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Patent Box: 10% effective CT rate on qualifying intraocular-lens patented income. Merged R&D Expenditure Credit: 20% repayable/offsettable credit on qualifying R&D (RDEC regime). Full Expensing & £1m Annual Investment Allowance on qualifying plant/machinery. No UK branch-profits or remittance tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No statutory time-limit: trading losses carry forward indefinitely (CTA 2010 s.45) subject to £5m unrestricted offset plus 50% of remaining profits restriction (CTA 2010 Part 7ZA). Capital losses also carry forward indefinitely. A multi-jurisdiction schema default of 5 years would be inaccurate for the UK.
